translations.text: i.e. 'O Corinthians': that is why he said 'multifariae' [?].
i.e. upon the commands of the law.
i.e. besides Corinth, or in every place where there are Christians besides.
'We pray': that is what he says, because it is two who have sent it, i.e. Paul and Sosthenes.
i.e. I marvel at God's grace among you.
i.e. through preaching, i.e. as it was preached to you, so you have accepted it.
i.e. it is among you all.
i.e. you have known the first coming through the gospel; you will know the second coming through revelation.
i.e. in the unity of the body of Christ, so that you too may be sons of God.
He gives them the name of brethren so that they may not say that the rebuke comes from hatred of them, but rather from love of them.

i.e. that you may have one faith. Here, then, he comes to the bitter salt of the rebuke, since up to now he has smeared the lips of the cup with honey, i.e. he has spoken gentle and friendly words to them.

i.e. that the faith that is in your hearts and what you say with your lips may be the same. Here, then, the reason for which the epistle was written is shown, i.e. the contentions and dissension that existed among them, among the disciples. There was unity, however, among their masters; they themselves were all servants of God. But the disciples made a distinction between them, and made gods of them; that is what he rebukes here.
i.e. some of it has been made known to me.
i.e. they are not contentions of the world.
i.e. these are the contentions that are among you.
Pelagius: The body is divided where the members dissent, i.e. giving the honour due to the head to the members.
i.e. it is to me myself that he will come first.
although, then, the worship due to God should be given to Paul in that way.
i.e. who say that they were not baptized in my name, i.e. that is not your position [?].
i.e. unless I baptized them.
apart from them
i.e. I do not remember whether I baptized anyone else.

i.e. as he said, 'that you may carry our name before the Gentiles'. Preaching, then, and converting were his task, so that everyone might be ready for baptism; and his disciples baptized them afterwards, so that he might not be hindered [?] by the thing that another could do.

i.e. in which you glory, i.e. it is not that I could not do it indeed, but the mystery of the cross will not be understood if the preaching is eloquent and brilliant. 'Cross', then, is a name for the act of crucifixion, but it is transferred from that to be a name for the tree.
i.e. they do not think it fitting that the Lord should be crucified, and it is foolishness [to them].
i.e. the Gentile will appear from among the Greeks, i.e. it will be seeking: they have sought [?] the school [?] before its revelation [?].
i.e. it is clear that it is not wisdom.
i.e. that is why I call it foolish.
i.e. to the elements, or whatever wisdom it is that is wisdom from God.
They did not understand it through their own wisdom.
i.e. they think preaching to them is no use unless miracles are done along with it.
i.e. they think it is no use unless it is eloquent.
i.e. we preach, i.e. I am not ashamed that they think it foolishness and a stumbling-block.

i.e. what people could not attain through their wisdom, he attained through his cross, i.e. what Jews and Greeks sought, i.e. power and wisdom, they would have found if they had believed, as those who are called have found it, etc.
i.e. all the faithful.
i.e. he will not be wise if it is according to the flesh.

i.e. are called, i.e. they are not all wise, i.e. not many of them are there; or, not many are powerful according to the flesh, for the one who is wise and powerful and strong and noble is the one who believes in Jesus Christ and in what he himself teaches.
i.e. he chose, i.e. those who do not have human wisdom.
i.e. from God the Father, not from anyone else.
It is in Jeremiah, or in this book.
i.e. so that the servant may have weakness and fear while he is serving his lord.
i.e. it was not in that that I instructed you [?], i.e. in philosophy.
Pelagius: with their wisdom, through our gospel; or, their bodies and their souls are separated from them; or, their wisdom is separated from them.
Pelagius: by the unbelievers, i.e. so that none of the wise of the world knows it.
i.e. wonderful things; or, a question, i.e. what is it that I have found?
i.e. the depths.
i.e. this is a comparison.
i.e. the understanding, i.e. except the person himself.
i.e. the person he is speaking about.
i.e. in that way the one in whom the Holy Spirit is knows the mysteries of God.
to the faithful
that is, we preach
that is, which we compare, i.e. his teaching, so that it may be suitable for everyone
that is, like a beast
that is, spiritual teaching is not fitting for him
that is, the other is despised by the spirit, i.e. by God or by a spiritual man
that is, no one casts contempt on him
that is, this is the sense: he teaches the knowledge of the Lord to everyone
that is, to men perfect in faith, i.e. it is not the teaching of the perfect that I teach you, for you would not endure that
that is, a gloss on 'as to carnal ones', i.e. you are not perfect in works in Christ
that is, not the teaching of strength
that is, this is why it would not be given to you
that is, for you are no better in the same way [?]
that is, carnal desires still oppress you
that is, this is what makes you carnal
that is, these are the contentions and rivalries
that is, what sort of men are you, if you make gods of them? i.e. they are servants and ministers of him in whom you have believed
that is, as they have been appointed for it
that is, they are not reckoned as anything
that is, it is he who is something
that is, it is fitting that you are cultivable
Pelagius: not according to my own power, i.e. it is through grace that I have endured it, then
that is, he to whom it has been preached builds upon it, i.e. it is not for me to build upon, but to lay the foundation
that is, it is fitting that the building be suited to the foundation
that is, though false apostles should lay [?] it
i.e. both good and bad.
i.e. if he is steadfast in tribulations and if his deed is good.
i.e. he who has built small sins.
i.e. loss, i.e. of reward, because he does not guard the flock well. [?] (dernum)
i.e. he will be saved, i.e. he will escape alone, separated from his flock.
i.e. in your steadfastness [?].
i.e. it will not be right to defile it.
i.e. you are that temple.
let him be [?].
i.e. let him be, i.e. let him make himself a fool.
i.e. dearer to him is he who has wisdom, i.e. with God.
i.e. no good is done through it.
i.e. I shall catch them, so that they may not be wise.
in craftiness, i.e. in cunning or in cleverness.
Pelagius: 'We are your ministers, but you are the people of Christ alone.' This is everything he says below.
i.e. the aforementioned, i.e. whatever [?] there is with him, it is all yours.
i.e. that is the same thing, and life.
i.e. that is the same thing, and death.
i.e. let this be the judgement that is passed on us.
i.e. [?] the divine mysteries.
i.e. this, then, is the good messenger: he who seeks glory for his lord and not for himself, i.e. that is what is sought there.
i.e. I think little of that importance: whether it is praise or reproach that you give me, I think little of its importance.
i.e. human praise is likened to the day because of how short it lasts, as the prophet says: 'I have not desired the day of men', that is, their praise.
i.e. the one who judges me, for good or for ill, is the Lord, i.e. it is God who knows what is in me.
I shall not be righteous on that account.
i.e. until the true judge comes.

i.e. fulfil what I preach: do not pass judgment on anyone among yourselves. As if he had said: this is why I have shown all these things that we said above in my own person, i.e. so that you may apply them to yourselves, and say that we are servants to you, and not boast of masters, such as Gamaliel, etc., and not judge anyone until the Lord judges him. Learn [?] humility from me, i.e. that you do not boast of masters and do not judge anyone, whether good or bad, until God judges him.
i.e. is it not you yourself? i.e. he is speaking to the puffed-up.
i.e. even if you had received this judgement as if from yourself, it would be no greater than [?] if you had received it.
i.e. you are not under our yoke.
i.e. I think.
i.e. as if we were condemned to death, i.e. like a man who goes into battle: he takes [?] an omen of death when he goes into battle.
i.e. to sinful Gentiles, i.e. something the eyes of the multitude see.
i.e. he preached by day, and laboured with his hands at night.
i.e. the fruit of his hand was what sustained him.
i.e. as if we were sweepings [?], i.e. for what is thrown out is cleansed; so the apostles are thrown out by men.
i.e. refuse, or perdition. Pelagius: peripsema is Greek and is interpreted as 'the worst' or 'the despised'.
i.e. up to this, i.e. up to the time we are in now.
i.e. perfect ones, for their perfecting [?].

i.e. their guardians, i.e. guardians of boys, i.e. people of mature age who look after children. Podos in Greek is pes ('foot') in Latin; gogos in Greek is tectum ('covering') in Latin. I.e. an attendant [?] who follows the teacher; or it is interpreted as 'guardian of the feet'.
i.e. though your teachers are many.
i.e. it is right for me to beseech you, since you are sons to me and I am your mother.
i.e. be like your father, i.e. take up your inheritance from your father and imitate his ways.
i.e. he imitates my ways.
i.e. a compound, i.e. fordub [?] likewise.
i.e. he will tell you, so that my ways may come [?] to you.
i.e. it is in Christ that those ways are.
i.e. as though I would not come to correct you; I will come indeed.
Pelagius: so that he might frighten them about his coming, i.e. their pride will come to an end [?] when I come.
i.e. I will find out how you will be.
i.e. 'a good work': that is what I would praise.
i.e. the choice lies with you, then: if it is better that you be corrected by another's correction, change your habits; if you change them, it is in love and in spirit that I shall come to you.
i.e. that would have been more fitting than being puffed up (inflatio).
i.e. so that he may not be in sin (in peccato) at all, but may be in penitence (in paenitentia).
i.e. he is present, then, when his words are read.
i.e. as though I were present.
i.e. it is not by my own authority that I have judged.
i.e. in the judgement of those letters (in earum litterarum iudicio); or, it is by that spirit that I have given judgement.

I have indeed judged to deliver such a man, or that you (vos) should deliver him. Otherwise: it is to madness that his delivery is said to be; it is through that that his soul will be saved in the day of the Lord, etc.
'of Satan', i.e. to the adversary, i.e. of penitence (paenitentiae), i.e. the virtue that comes in its place is the opposite of the vice.
i.e. so that his soul may be saved.
i.e. that you have not been able to pass judgement on this crime.
i.e. leaven.
i.e. unleavened, i.e. without the bitterness of sin.
i.e. just as leaven in bread was forbidden at the solemnity of the lamb, so (sic) it is not right for the leaven of sin to be at the solemnity of the Lamb, i.e. of Christ.
i.e. at the feast of Christ.
vanities
i.e. simplicity with us, and truth, as Adam was (ut fuit Adam) before sin.

'not at all with fornicators' (non utique fornicariis), i.e. I think that more notable to say, because I knew that you would not be in fellowship with such a man; otherwise you ought to (alioquin debueratis) [go out of the world], for their ways are not like yours; what is proper for you is not to be together.

i.e. it is for this reason that I wrote (scripsi). Pelagius: 'It would have been better for us to depart from this light than to be unworthily separated from fellowship through communion with the gentiles.'

i.e. it is not that I wrote to you (scripsi vobis), i.e. 'do not mingle' (non commisceamini), i.e. I do not tell you to separate from them, i.e. from the gentiles, because of preaching to them, to see whether they may be brought under the faith. Otherwise (alioquin), i.e. for if it were not for the sake of that preaching, you ought to (debueratis) go out of the land and the earth. That is not so; the order of preaching binds you, then, so that you should not go.
i.e. this time, i.e. I do not regret what I wrote (quod scripsi); I say it still.
i.e. [?] or despoiler.
It is thus.
i.e. a meal with him in a house, or accepting his food.
i.e. though he finds; i.e. he finds nothing.
i.e. it is 'brother' that I say; 'quid enim' etc.
This, in my opinion, is a 'beim foris' [?] upon what he said before; or it is a heading for what follows.
i.e. they have a judge apart from you, i.e. Christ.
i.e. he has dared; i.e. there is another evil among you.
i.e. a case or a lawsuit.
a lawsuit.
i.e. is judged.
i.e. it is not people of the Church who are judges among you.
i.e. if you had known, you would not take the petty judgements before them.
Pelagius: through you or by your example; i.e. it will be through your power that this world will be judged.

'We shall judge', i.e. [?] the angels, i.e. demons; because sin is more natural [?] for us, though we sin, coming from the frail substance of the flesh in which we were born, than it was for him from the subtle substance in which he was born; therefore we shall judge him, etc. Or we shall judge the true angels; i.e. this indeed is the way we shall judge them: i.e. as they will be around the judgement, so we too shall be, as it says: 'He shall call the heaven from above and the earth, to judge his people.' Or it is said of Christ, who in our human nature will judge the angels. Or the more exalted saints will judge the lower.
[?] who are doing penance in the churches.
i.e. let it be they who give judgements among you.
to put you to shame, i.e. that you may blush.
i.e. it is that no wise man appears, since it is thus that it is done.
i.e. that, however, is what you do.
i.e. by a lawsuit.
i.e. this order was not yours, but it belonged to the unbelievers.
i.e. even certainly.
i.e. this is the reproach: it is one sin upon another, i.e. fornication first, and then lawsuits, you who ought always to have kept peace, even at the loss of temporal things.
i.e. what hinders you from forgiving every injury that might be done to you, without pursuing a claim for it?
i.e. it would be better than avenging it.
i.e. you do not forgive the injury that is done to you, but you sue for it.
i.e. you withhold from everyone and you defraud everyone.
i.e. a deed, i.e. it would not be the same for you even if it were he against whom you did it.
i.e. in his view, these are the 'enemies': those who defraud and those who do wrong.
i.e. those who lie with [males].
i.e. those who curse others, i.e. people who are given to slandering.
i.e. [?] so none of these will be in the unity of the household of heaven.
i.e. names or deeds: so all this was a name for you, or you did all this.

i.e. that purity, holiness and righteousness come to you through the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and through the Holy Spirit. So here he names the three persons, i.e. the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
i.e. I will not be brought under the power of any of the desires, as drunkards are brought under the power of wine, and the like.
i.e. it is close to its kin.
i.e. food, i.e. it is not the person that the Godhead [?] destroys by that.
i.e. it will be plain to them there.
i.e. [?] … so he says this here in order to [?] restrain the foods, i.e. to forbid lust, for if there were no gluttony there would be no lust.
i.e. so that the Lord is ruler over it; it is the custom of a ruler to protect and to punish.
i.e. because we are his members, i.e. the body whose ruler is the Lord will be raised up through the power of the Godhead, just as the Lord Jesus was raised up.
i.e. that I should take members away from Christ and make them the members of a harlot? Far from it.

i.e. for the harlot gathers to herself the sins of all who come to her, so that what is spoken of is one body of sin, and it is called the body of that great mass of sins. And whoever goes to her gathers onto himself the great mass of that body and of that sin which is on the harlot, and yet it does not leave her; instead it grows in both of them.
i.e. avoid it, and be quick about it, for it is right to avoid it.
i.e. except lust.
i.e. it produces a body for him, i.e. the body of the sins that are on the harlot.
i.e. I am sure that you would not commit lust if you knew this.
i.e. from the Godhead.
i.e. you do not belong to yourselves.
let it be he [?] … [?]
i.e. that would be more fitting for you than for there to be sins in your possession there.
i.e. questions, for letters had been sent from them to him with their questions.
i.e. this is the answer you should take from me.
i.e. she cannot refuse marital union unless it is the husband's will.
i.e. unless it is pleasing to the husband.
i.e. so let the husband not boast, then, that he has the power now, because he too cannot refuse marital union unless it is the will "of the woman".
of the two works
i.e. let neither refuse the other, i.e. "by reason of marriage".
i.e. except only.
i.e. unless you both agree to it.
i.e. so that no one may leave his lawful bond for adultery through the will of the devil and through your lack of self-control.
i.e. if what happened in this were my wish, everyone would be as I am, i.e. in virginity. "Here virginity is shown."
i.e. between virginity and marriage.
i.e. and even if I wish it, perhaps they would not all be equal. But even if they are not like me in virginity, they will all be in the will of God.
Pelagius: "Here begins another matter, concerning widows", i.e. let them live in chastity.
Jerome: "Therefore it is better to marry than to burn, which is worse." This is an evil that is better than an evil.
i.e. this is what I command.
i.e. if she separates from her husband, she may not go to another man, but let her live in chastity.
i.e. if she wants to go to a man, let it be the same husband.
i.e. this does not rest with me; rather, "it is the Lord" who "says that a wife should not depart from her husband".
i.e. he is pleased to live with her.
i.e. let her not separate from the husband, in case he may be saved through living with her.
i.e. this is [?]. That is why I say that they should stay together, in case one of the two may be saved through the other.
"Otherwise", i.e. if it is not so, the children will be unclean, i.e. what comes from the unbeliever will be an unbeliever.
i.e. "the children": because you are together and one of you is now a believer, the children are believers too.
i.e. let the believer not hold him back, and let him not give in to him.
i.e. so that we may have no quarrel with anyone.
i.e. you will save the husband, even though he is with you against his will.
i.e. O man, how do you know whether you will save the woman, even though she is with you against her will?
i.e. as the Lord has distributed to each one, whether with a spouse or in virginity.
i.e. whether in virginity or in marriage, as he has been called, let him be so. This is the heading of the law in front, though it might be said that it would be a blow against the aforesaid law.
i.e. that is the instruction to everyone.
i.e. virginity, i.e. circumcised from marriage; for it is not carnal circumcision that he means here, since virginity circumcises vices.
i.e. let him not enter into marriage. It is clear here that what was said above is not about carnal circumcision. Or: let his mind not seek the foreskin if he is circumcised.
i.e. let him not put away his wife; or let his mind not [?] reject it, though that would be better.
i.e. it is not enough for you to be without a wife unless you do good works.
i.e. whatever grade one is in, whether in virginity or in marriage, it is necessary to fulfil God's commandment in it.
i.e. without changing.
i.e. do not seek virginity.
i.e. though you are able to put your wife away from you, she is not to be put away; but wait to see whether there is mutual consent between you.
i.e. it is in marriage that he has been called to God.
i.e. a freedman, i.e. he is a free companion to God, who does not serve [him] only.
i.e. he serves Christ only, i.e. without half-service to a spouse.
i.e. let him remain in it still, but let it be in accordance with God's will.
i.e. it is not this that he said: that one should be in virginity whether one is able or not able. Question: what did the Lord say? Not difficult: 'He who can receive it, let him receive it.'
i.e. for if he had given a command, the penalty for transgressing it would have followed.
i.e. so that it may help you against the [?] (coming necessity?) when it comes.
i.e. if it was with your wife that you believed, do not separate from her after believing.
i.e. if it was not with a wife that you believed, do not take a wife after believing.
i.e. the troubles of the world will not be taken from them, i.e. bearing and rearing [children]; and what they have of rest from it is loss of reward [?].
i.e. that you should be in virginity.
i.e. this is the end of the world; it is not worth giving love to it. Or: this is a [?] 'that those who have', i.e. this is what remains: 'that those who', etc.
i.e. as a daughter and father, or sister and brother, are.
i.e. as if they did not possess, or, so that they may be like those who do not possess wives.
i.e. like those who do not weep, or, as if they did not weep.
i.e. like those who do not buy.
i.e. as if they did not use the world.
i.e. he has no care except service to God, and that is what would be proper.
i.e. he has no care except service to his wife (uxori).
i.e. each of the two has a different order (ordo), i.e. the wife (mulier) and the unmarried woman (innubta).
i.e. that is, the virgin.
i.e. it is she whom he speaks of below.
Pelagius: "I do not impose necessity on the unwilling", i.e. it is not to force virginity on you, but to offer you a reward.
i.e. this, then, is the honestum: praying to God without any hindrance from the cares of the world, i.e. from wives.
i.e. it is unseemly through the concupiscence of sin.
i.e. she has come of age [?].
i.e. as the girl desires.
i.e. so both things are drawn from this text.
i.e. he has resolved in his heart that the girl should remain in virginity, or, to keep her in her former state.

Here, then, he shows the difference between marriage and virginity: marriage is said 'not to sin' (non peccare) and virginity 'to do well' (benefacere); and when marriage is said 'to do well' (benefacere), virginity is 'to do better' (melius facere).
i.e. she has been released from service to a husband.
i.e. as long as the husband is alive.
i.e. I would prefer, however, that she remain in virginity.
i.e. the Spirit of God is in me; it would be better to follow my counsel.
i.e. that an idol is nothing and that it does not [?] anything.
i.e. that knowledge, however, would be good, provided there were no pride in it; but pride is in it, and it is not living [?].
i.e. indulgence toward the brother who is weak in faith, so that it builds him up in faith.

i.e. this is how it would be right for one who has knowledge of the idols. But let him not eat the offerings made to the idol, so that brotherly love is not destroyed by giving offence to the believing brother who is weak of mind.
i.e. it is then that God knows him, through indulgence toward the weak brother.

'In conscience', i.e. their conscience is weak, and they find what is offered to idols abhorrent [?]. But the strong one encourages them to eat that food, and it is the same for them as if it were idolothyte [food offered to idols] that they were eating, because they do not eat it through strength of faith.
i.e. it is the same for them as if it were idolothyte.
'Stumbling-block', i.e. they find it offensive that it is given to them or that it is done in their presence.
i.e. for he eats the food that was on the altar of the idol.
i.e. is it not?
i.e. having a conscience.
i.e. he will be emboldened. Does he not say, 'I will eat idolothyte, since he who is better than I eats it'?
i.e. it is a small thing for you to make allowance for him; it is for him that Christ suffered.
i.e. since Christ died for the sake of the weak folk, and they are therefore members of Christ, the offence that is done to them is done to Christ.
i.e. it is as if it were Christ who was offended.
i.e. since what the brother thinks bad is an offence to Christ, i.e. if it causes my brother to deny [the faith].
i.e. that I may not [?] him, i.e. that denial [of the faith] may not be caused to him.
Is it not?
i.e. since I am an apostle and a teacher to everyone, am I not free to do any deed?
i.e. my soul-friend is good.
i.e. O Corinthians, i.e. is it not I who brought you to faith in the Lord?
i.e. a sign.

i.e. even if I am not an apostle of the peoples in your opinion, Corinthians, and in that of the Gentiles who have not believed, it is indeed an apostle's work that brought this about, and it is I who preached to them.

i.e. it would be the fruit of labour for us in this way, even if we ate every food and did what our companions do, except that it would not be a strengthening of the brethren and an expectation of greater reward.
i.e. that there should be women ministering to us; it would not be refused to us, any more than to another [?].
i.e. a question, i.e. is it likely that there should be a special servitude for me and Barnabas?
i.e. the three things he said above, [?] that we have power: 'for who goes to war...'
i.e. it would be a reward for his labour even if he ate it.
i.e. these examples are human, then, or not carnal; and I do not speak according to man but according to spiritual sense, i.e. not through man but through Jesus Christ.
i.e. Do you not say it? No — it says it.
i.e. who threshes, i.e. for it is a custom with them that the oxen thresh the corn.
i.e. That is likelier, i.e. it is we who are the oxen, who plough the land of men's hearts.
i.e. what the Law says, 'You shall not muzzle,' etc., i.e. it is not about the ox in the literal, historical sense; rather, these two things were said of us preachers: 'because in hope,' etc.
i.e. if we have preached to you.
Is it great, i.e. is it too much?
i.e. it is no perversion [?] for you that spiritual things go from us to you and carnal things from you to us.
i.e. would it not have been more fitting to give it to us?
i.e. so that it may not be said that the preaching is only for the sake of food, and so that the believers may not be offended with us, and so that I may have a reward.

i.e. the place where the high priests used to pray, i.e. in the Holy of Holies.
i.e. the due of a priest in the temple: it was to them that it used to be given.
i.e. those are the Levites as well, who used to serve at the offerings.

i.e. as that law was in the Old Testament, so is this in the New Testament.
i.e. the honours that are given for preaching the gospel.
i.e. the glory that will be given to me in heaven.
i.e. through the reward for my preaching being given to me.
i.e. if I preach for reward, i.e. for my food and my sustenance, I shall have no reward after my preaching.
i.e. preaching is necessary for my food and my sustenance; if I do not preach, I shall die of cold and hunger.
Unless you declare to the wicked man his wickedness; or: it will be woe to me through cold and hunger if I do not preach.
i.e. if it is my own will that drives me to it, not for reward.
i.e. it is a commercial bargain if it is preached for reward, i.e. that is what has been granted to me for my sustenance.

i.e. without reward.

i.e. so that they might be wealth in the faith, or so that they might be a treasure of reward for me.
i.e. in circumcising the disciple, i.e. I was a Jew in appearance.
i.e. I was not a Jew in my customs.
i.e. so that I might bring them to the faith.
i.e. as he brought testimony from the altars of the idols to show them the God who was hidden [?], i.e. of the true God, as he said: 'I saw an altar on which was written: To the unknown God.'
i.e. through indulgence toward them.
i.e. it is for this that I was all things to all.
in a race-course
i.e. they all run, and it is one man of them who wins the victory in completing it.

No one will be deprived of his labour, i.e. it will not be only one of you who will win the victory.
i.e. so that he may be readier for the victory.
i.e. the plate.

Question: why should the rock be spiritual? Not hard to answer: because it figures Christ, the cornerstone. That is the mystical rock from which flowed the great stream of spiritual teaching, which quenched the spiritual thirst of the saints of Israel in the desert of the world as they sought the land of promise of the living.
i.e. although God did much good to them.
i.e. not all of them were chosen.
i.e. vengeance fell upon them; if they had been chosen, it would not have reached them.
i.e. not all the children of Israel were evil.
i.e. we should not desire what they desired; [it is] for our salvation.

i.e. after what he had endured.

in the end ... [?] ... and in the [?] ... perfection may be given.
let him beware.

profit, or increase.

i.e. this, then, is the human temptation he spoke of above: the worship of idols and the desire for their food.

in the market-house [?]

i.e. in return for the eating of the creatures.
i.e. this, then, is the concluding stroke on it.
i.e. it is to the glory of God, and it is strength of faith, to go along with the one who is weak in faith.
i.e. going along with their outward ways, without going along with their habits unless they are good.

so that the imitation of Christ might not be too great for them all at once.

With veiled head, i.e. it was their custom to veil their heads during prayers and preaching; or, their being without a crown (tonsure?): that is the veiling he speaks of.

i.e. for it is the same, i.e. being bareheaded, i.e. as if she were shorn, i.e. by her husband, or of her hair.

i.e. as Christ is the head of the man, the man is the head of the woman; as the woman gives honour [?] to the man, so does the man to Christ.

i.e. it is certain that they will exist, and it is this that will bring schisms to completion, etc.

It would be [?] for you if you had done it otherwise, without any great excess.
i.e. or [?] the church that they make [of it]. Pelagius: making it a banqueting hall.

Gregory: so that they would not think the Lord's body was common bread, he strongly threatens those who receive it unworthily, i.e. it is crucifying Christ again when one takes the body of Christ unworthily.
i.e. Pelagius: conscience must be examined to see whether it reproaches us in nothing, i.e. we must be cleansed through penance, so that there may be nothing in which our conscience convicts us.
i.e. but let him have no sins.
i.e. weakness of his whole body.
i.e. [?], i.e. members are missing from them; or, those members are dead though they are in the body.
i.e. they die an untimely death, i.e. shortness of life.
i.e. to correct us.
i.e. let each wait for the other.
i.e. for the sacrifice is not enough for him; but if it is not enough, let him not eat in church, but at home.
i.e. if you make a banqueting-house [?] of the church.
i.e. I would rather that you knew, nevertheless.
i.e. it is clear to you.
i.e. because you were like idols, i.e. for you did not grasp the knowledge of Christ in that, i.e. for you did not know.
i.e. 'first to the gods' [?], i.e. it will not be in the Spirit of God that he says it.
i.e. the graces of the Holy Spirit, however, are many, though the Spirit is one.
He gives three names to the Spirit here, i.e. Spirit and Lord and God; it is shown here that it is the work of nothing else but of the Spirit.
i.e. the Spirit is manifested in him through the grace that He gives him.
i.e. moreover it is one Spirit who distributes it.
Pelagius: so that he may cure the sick, as physicians do; or the working of miracles.
i.e. translating from one language into another, as Jerome and the Seventy did; or drawing out mysteries from single words and then preaching from them, as is the custom of preachers.
i.e. 'Spirit': it is shown that the gifts of the Spirit are many and that the Spirit is one.
This, then, is a comparison he makes, i.e. just as each member serves another in the body, so the talent of each of you should serve another, for we are one body in Christ.
Those members are one body, though they are many.
i.e. it is one body with Christ, i.e. the saints and the just.
i.e. we have been joined together into one body through baptism.
i.e. they are all in that body, i.e. Jews and Gentiles.
i.e. it is you who have drunk deeply of the grace of the Holy Spirit.

i.e. for they are members that make up a body.

i.e. It is not that it would not be of the body on that account; rather, it is of it.
If in the Church, then, the foot is the people of the active life, and the hand is the people of an active life that is greater than the other.
i.e. the people of the contemplative life.

i.e. he has indeed formed one body out of many members.
i.e. "I have no need of the feet," etc.
i.e. it is not merely that each member does not need another; rather, much more, etc.
i.e. those that are weak, such as the heart and the liver and other internal organs, or the male and female parts.
i.e. their protection: it is [?] better for them that the other members should serve them than that they should serve themselves, even if it were in their power.
i.e. through the service of the other members to them, i.e. gathering clothing about them and food for them.
i.e. the face and the hands and the feet.
i.e. of honour, i.e. what was lacking to it, i.e. the colour and vigour that the whole body brings about: that is in it.
i.e. that each member should do what pleases another, since they are in one body; let their unity be good.
i.e. as they [?].
i.e. since it is one body, let each member help another.

i.e. if the member is healthy after its sickness, it is a comfort to the other members.

i.e. it is clear, then, why the comparison has been brought this far: i.e. just as there is unity among the members of a human body, so there should be unity among us too, since we are the body of Christ and we are the members of the body of Christ.
i.e. it is they who have taken pre-eminence, because the apostles saw what the prophets prophesied.
i.e., people who give spiritual direction (soul-friendship), teaching only in the present.
i.e., those who do special deeds, or the working of miracles.

Step by step, nearer and nearer, he has come to himself.

A wallet, i.e., relief, i.e., in food and clothing.
i.e. but only the love of God.

i.e. we shall not speak, i.e. but their charity will be held in common [?] in the same way.
i.e. it is little that we have known of the mysteries of God.
i.e. it is little that we preach of the mysteries of God, for we do not know them.
i.e. our being in the future, i.e. the future life, or full knowledge.
i.e. when I was.
i.e. since perfection has come to me, I do not do childish deeds; but when we reach heaven we shall be wise and we shall all be perfect.
i.e. he compares this to the sight of the eye.
i.e. this is how we see the divine mysteries: as someone sees a thing through a shadow, while we are in the body.
i.e. for what is seen through darkness is not clear and is not certain.
i.e. it is in part that I have known, or it is a part of me that has known in part, i.e. only the soul has known it.
i.e. that, however, will be wholly; it will not be in part.

i.e. even if it is in the present life.
i.e. the gifts of charity, i.e. the three above: hope, faith, charity.
they teach
i.e. the one who speaks many languages.
i.e. for they do not understand.
i.e. if he understands it [?].

i.e. who preaches.
i.e. that is a benefit.
i.e. that is a benefit to himself alone.
i.e. he himself understands, or it brings praise to him.
i.e., preaching.
That is, that is a benefit to many.
That is, it is not out of envy toward you that I say this, for I would like you to speak many tongues.
That is, that, however, would be better in my view.
That is, so I prefer what brings that great power to you.
Only, it is a benefit on this condition: that he interpret what he says and bring it to everyone's understanding.
That is, so that many may be built up through it.
That is, through many tongues.
That is, I will now give you an example that will fit your case.
That is, what good will it do you if it is spoken in that way?
That is, so that it may be clear to everyone.
That is, so that everyone may know.
Or prophecy, that is, in preaching, that is, stirring someone up to faith so that he may be ready for baptism.
That is, teaching someone after his baptism.
That is, a pipe.
That is, a harp.
That is, unless there is a distinction in the sound, their measures are not understood.
That is, what is played on the pipe or the harp.
Or, what is harped.

This is another comparison of his, that is, the comparison of a trumpet. A trumpet has many calls, and each one is different: one for battle, another for feasting, or for marching, or for sleep, or for council. Unless the man who plays it makes them distinct, that is, if he plays only one measure, no one understands what it is being sounded for. In the same way, unless a foreign language is made distinct and interpreted, whoever hears it does not understand it.
That is, the latter is like you.
That is, unless you interpret.
That is, 'into the air', that is, a Greek accusative. That is, it will be a striking of the air for you, for no one will understand what you say.
That is, though it may not be clear to you, there are many kinds of language in this world.
That is, there is no language without sound. That is, then what use is that sound to you unless you know what lies beneath that sound?
i.e. for he does not understand the language I speak; he will then say: "This is a barbarian."
i.e. since it is so, then, i.e. that preaching is better than speaking many languages, let that be what you do.
i.e. let him be eloquent in such a way that he may interpret.
i.e. let him be eloquent, or: let him pray to God that he may interpret, i.e. that the sense may be understood.
i.e. though he be eloquent
i.e. my mind, however, does not understand, i.e. because I do not understand what I speak.
i.e. what, then, is good for us? Not hard to say: I will speak eloquently with the spirit and with the mind, i.e. my mind will understand what my lips say.
i.e. though you say it with the sound only
i.e. though he fill
i.e. a proper place, or a place of manifestation and revelation, for it does not profit him unless it is made plain to him.
i.e. to the foolish man, or to the common [?] man
i.e. the purport [?] of the teaching that you speak
i.e. he will not know where it is fitting to say Amen.
i.e. it is not easy for him to say Amen in that way.
i.e. it is shown, however, through the fair declaration, that you have the grace of God, but it does not profit anyone else.
i.e. so that they should not think, then, that speaking many languages was not a grace of the Spirit, he says this.
i.e. I am able, then, to interpret them.
i.e. the sense from which I desire the salvation of everyone
i.e. however it may be, then, he says, I thank, but in the church, etc.
i.e. this is the perfect in preference to the imperfect, i.e. rather than ten thousand words in speaking many languages and my not understanding them so that I might preach them.
i.e. that was said, then, for the sake of the imperfect; do not you be imperfect, then, for it is not fitting for you.
i.e. he will know every language when he is carried into captivity.
i.e. though they have heard many languages and though they speak them, they will not be the better for it; it is clear, then, that speaking many languages is not of great force.
i.e. this, then, is the only profit for which speaking many languages is given: that God may be marvelled at through it, and that unbelievers may be readier to believe.
i.e. to the preacher
That is, preaching, however, is for the faithful.
That is, he is still forbidding the covetousness.
That is, without the profit of preaching.
That is, foolish or unbelieving.
Or at the time [?].
That is, this is what they will say: these people are mad.
That is, if they preach.
That is, judgement is passed on him.
That is, it is through the preaching that everyone's conduct is shown, and those habits do not withstand it, namely deed and word and thought.
That is, every one of these men is a prophet.
That is, what is to be done about that, then? It is not difficult: let each take his psalm and teach and reveal whatever anyone has, so that it may be for edification.
Pelagius: the understanding of the psalm, that is, understanding what the psalm sings.
That is, after baptism.
That is, memory, that is, the revealing of mysteries.
That is, speaking many languages, with translation into another language.
That is, his languages into a language.
That is, whatever gift is given to anyone, then, let him use it for the edification of the church, that is, the edification of many in the faith.
That is, if there is anyone there, then, who speaks many languages, let there not be more than two or three, then.
That is, let them speak, that is, but let each speak after the other, that is, let them not speak at the same time.
That is, let it be one man who preaches it, for rivalry [?] between the two is unseemly; or let one man interpret the three in that way.
That is, for he will not understand.
That is, to himself only.
That is, it is enough for a preacher in the church; let the other disciples and learners come, each after the other.
That is, you will all be able to be preachers through this taking of turns, if each of you gives way to the other.
That is, let them listen to the preaching and pass judgement on it, because it is a custom among them [?] of preachers.
That is, if there is any of the mysteries that comes into the mind of the man who is sitting, and he rises.
His fellow, i.e. he who was master before, so that he may be disciple afterwards.

This is his answer to their thoughts, in case anyone should say so, when he says 'For you can all prophesy one by one' etc.: i.e. everyone will be a teacher there, for that is how you will be able to prophesy, if it is one by one. A question, then: what about the women, what will they do? Will they preach? No, says Paul: 'let them keep silent' etc.
i.e. let them keep silent indeed, i.e. in all things that are held in common.
i.e. in all things that are preached.

i.e. some say, then, that it was the Holy Spirit that was in the prophets of the Old Testament, and that it should be subject to the prophets of the New, i.e. to the apostles. That is not true, for he is not speaking of them here, but of the preachers.
i.e. everyone owes humility to one another.
i.e. he is a God of peace and of concord [?].
i.e. if there are men present, for it is unfitting for the member to correct anything that the head says.
i.e. it is clear, then, that the man who preached this and his fellow did not want anyone to come after him, as if indeed it had come not from you but from apostles.
i.e. as if it had been preached to you alone; it was not to you only, but to all nations. 'Or did it come from you?', i.e. it is not fitting [?] to make a world [?] out of the gospel.
i.e. let his mind be set on this, that he should preach in the same way.
i.e. though it is my part to write them, they are the Lord's, however.
i.e. the bestowal of grace is from God.
i.e. not in pretence [?], but let it be as I say.
i.e. provided that those languages are interpreted.
i.e. by themselves or by the others.
So here he permits the like of preaching and speaking in many tongues, provided it is for the profit of the church.
i.e. let every deed be done in its proper way.

i.e. let everything you do be modest and fitting, whether preaching or speaking in tongues; let it be done as I say. This is a rebuke of the irregularities mentioned before, or else it is the heading for the irregularity that follows.
i.e. accept, then, my preaching.
i.e. that is praise for them.
i.e. may you fulfil it in the same way that it was preached to you.
i.e. it would be fitting [?], even though you do not fulfil it; much [?] has been preached to you.
i.e. unless the faith you have believed is in vain.
i.e. the thing you doubt, i.e. the resurrection, is what I made known to you before everything.
That is, as the prophets foretold, as it was prefigured in the Law, and as it is told in the Gospel.
… so this vision was shown to the five hundred … [?] who were in the city at that time.
That is, more than five hundred men, to confirm the resurrection (resurrectionis).
That is, alive (in uita): if you want even to speak with any of them, you could do so.
That is, by me.
That is, for apostleship is a great honour, that is, being under the teaching [?] of Jesus.
That is, it is the grace of God that has enabled me, so that I am an apostle with you.
That is, not without works (non sine operibus): what it did for me was not in vain.
That is, though I was the least (minimus) and though I was one born out of due time (abortivus).
That is, our teaching is one, since we have one grace.
That is, as we preached to you, so you have believed.
That is, even this is a reproach to them, that is, their ignorance [?] without preaching [?].

That is, if the preaching that I have preached is clear to you, namely that Christ rose from the dead, why do you allow a part of you to say [?] that there is no resurrection of men (de resurrectione hominum)?

That is, this is a habit of the clever: they let the contest [?] go on ahead of them, and then they strike in behind it [?] once they have got a sense of the course, so that afterwards they run ahead of the others.
That is, what we preach is futile and empty for us if it is not true, as they say.
That is, in that case we bear false witness about God.
That is, that testimony is against him.
That is, we charge God with something that he did not do in that way, namely the raising of Christ.
That is, the reason I charge them with denying the resurrection of Christ is that they deny the resurrection of the dead (resurrectionem mortuorum).
That is, it is evident that if you do not believe in the resurrection of Christ and of the dead, your faith will not sanctify you in that way and will not separate you from your sins.
That is, it is death for them if there is no eternal life.
That is, if what we believe in is only the life of Christ here, or if it is only for our life here.
That is, more than anyone.
That is, that, however, is true, and the resurrection of all after him is also true.
That is, 'firstfruits' (primitiae) is a plural noun. He is the firstfruits in magnificence [?] in the resurrection and in receiving glory.
i.e. this, then, is a likeness of comparison [?].
resurget ['will rise'], i.e. this is not to set an order in the resurrection, for all the dead will rise together.
i.e. in the order in which the righteous receive reward, and in the order in which sinners receive punishment.
i.e. there will be an end to the service of every element, for it will not be needed thereafter.
i.e. it is then indeed that the end will be, when the Son gives back to the Father those whom he has ruled until now.
i.e. he will bring them under the power of the Son.
i.e. ancient names for the demons, for every rank among them sinned [?].
i.e. whichever death that is, whether the death of the separation of body and soul or the death of punishment, etc.
i.e. lest it be thought that the Godhead would be subject to the manhood.
i.e. it is he alone who will be [all] [?].
i.e. for sins that bring about death [?], or for sinners who before death had the desire for baptism.
i.e. at all.

He shows three things here, i.e. a difference between heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, a difference among the heavenly bodies themselves, and a difference among the earthly bodies themselves. The difference among the heavenly bodies signifies the difference in the glory of the saints in heaven. The difference among the earthly bodies signifies the difference in the punishments that sinners will have in hell.
